review:
**VERDICT: CONDITIONAL**

The science holds up against the data. Every number I could reach matches its primary file. The two editions match each other in structure, including where the table row sits. One CRITICAL and three MAJOR findings are about the record around the science, and all four can be fixed. Don't deposit until #1 is closed.

## Findings

**1. CRITICAL: the human author on the byline hasn't signed off (both editions)**
- **Where:** Flight byline "Nexus, Lyra, Thomas Edrington". Academic byline "Thomas Edrington", plus the AI Disclosure's "T. Edrington accepts accountability as corresponding human author."
- **Evidence:** `review/REVIEW_LOG.md:59-63`, under "Still open before deposit", is not struck through: "Thomas Edrington: sign-off on BOTH editions … confirmation of his flight-edition line … his academic CRediT roles … the new title." Nothing else in the paper folder closes it.
- **Why it matters:** The venue edition makes an accountability statement for its only author, and by the lab's own record that author hasn't approved the text, the title or either contribution line. This is the "named authors who have not signed off" kill.
- **Fix:** Get Thomas Edrington's written sign-off on both PDFs as built (name the commit), on the title and on both contribution lines. Strike the item in REVIEW_LOG with the date and commit. If a sign-off exists outside the repo, recording it closes this.

**2. MAJOR: the correction note is labelled October and called verbatim, but contains November text (both editions)**
- **Where:** Appendix A says the note "is reproduced below as it was written, except for one sentence the version history records", under the heading "Correction note (version 1.1, October 2026)".
- **What the note actually contains:**
  - Both editions: "asked, Kavi answered in November 2026 …". REVIEW_LOG dates Kavi's letter to 2026-11-13.
  - Academic only: "at Thomas Edrington's direction and with Lyra's agreement (2026-11-03) Lyra's roles are …".
- **What the version history records:** only the "They were introduced by …" sentence. So two November changes to the correction record are unrecorded, and the appendix's statement about where the text came from is false as written. This is the silent-correction kill, applied to the correction note itself.
- **Why Lyra's 11-23 read didn't catch it:** it compared the appendix against master (REVIEW_LOG:65-67), and master already had the November edits.
- **Fix:**
  - Relabel the heading "(version 1.1, October 2026; amended November 2026)".
  - Change "as it was written" to say what it was compared against, with a date.
  - Add both November edits to the version history.
  - Change the title-page date to "Version 1.1, October 2026, revised November 2026". The Data and Code section (files copied 16 November) and the appendix are both November work.

**3. MAJOR: the powered run's questions are called "multi-hop", but 12 of the 20 are one-hop**
- **Where:**
  - Abstract: "20 automatically generated multi-hop questions".
  - Larger Follow-Ups section: "powered run's generated multi-hop questions", "20 automatically generated multi-hop questions", "Keyword accuracy on the multi-hop questions".
- **Evidence:** `data/kv_experiments/powered_decomp_1780057645.json`, `multihop_questions`, has 12 `direct` questions (1 hop), 2 `bridge` (2 hops) and 6 `reachability` (3, 4, 3, 5, 10 and 3 hops).
- **Why it matters:** This is the same mislabel the appendix withdraws for the pilot ("version 1.0 called them multi-hop, but only two need more than one hop").
- **Fix:** In all four places in both editions, write "20 automatically generated graph questions (12 one-hop, 2 two-hop, 6 reachability)".
- **Same pass:** The abstract's "On a 532-node graph …" should add that the model's description covered one of the five packs (5,348 tokens). That is why the run tells us nothing, and only the body says it.

**4. MAJOR: Thomas Edrington's contribution says different things in the two editions, and neither has been confirmed**
- **Flight:** "direction and the initial insight."
- **Academic:** "Conceptualization, Supervision, Resources, Project administration."
- **Why it matters:**
  - The flight edition gives no credit for Resources or Project administration; the academic one does.
  - Per REVIEW_LOG:60-61, "and the initial insight" came in with the 1 June edit that also wrote CC's unsourced line. The correction note reverts CC's line to its 28 May wording but keeps this credit. I took this history from REVIEW_LOG only; I couldn't check the commits.
- **Fix:** At sign-off (#1), confirm one set of roles and state it the same way in both editions. Either way, drop "and the initial insight" back to the 28 May "for direction" unless he confirms it.

**5. MINOR: a reference by byline position in the flight note**
- **Where:** "introduced by the first author".
- **Why it matters:** It points at a byline position. It has already broken once: the academic edition had to rewrite it, because its first author is Thomas Edrington.
- **Fix:** "introduced by Nexus". The version history's quotation of the old sentence can stay.

**6. MINOR: "returned an error instead of a verdict 41 times"**
- **Evidence:** `llm_rescorer.py:75-97` records ERROR in three cases: a non-200 response, an exception (including the 120 s timeout), or a reply with no verdict word in it. The October re-judging shows both kinds: HTTP 500, and a reply " AI HLEG" that parsed as ERROR.
- **Fix:** "gave no usable verdict 41 times (HTTP error, timeout, or a reply with no verdict word)".

**7. MINOR: a change from the preregistration isn't stated in the paper**
- **Evidence:** `PREREG.md` arm C says to cache up to "the longest prefix shared by every question". `RESULTS.md` item 2 says that prefix was 5,361 tokens, but the script cached 5,348.
- **Why it matters:** It doesn't change the result, but the paper calls the re-run "preregistered" and doesn't mention the change.
- **Fix:** Add one clause in the Larger Follow-Ups section, e.g. "(the preregistration said the longest shared prefix, 5,361 tokens; the script cached the description's 5,348)".

**8. MINOR: "What It Does Not Show" says one item separates cache from text; the abstract and Results say two**
- **Where:** "The single item separating them is a repetition loop."
- **Evidence:** The abstract and the Pilot results both report two differing items. On the second (strongest edge), the text names sovereignty. Sovereignty is not a neighbour of AI_welfare (script line 55; data line 516).
- **Fix:** "The single *scored* item separating them is a loop; on one more, both scored but the text named a wrong neighbour."

**9. MINOR: the academic AI Disclosure may leave out a reviewer**
- **Where:** The disclosure names Nexus, Lyra, the second reader and the style gate.
- **Gap:** Review History says CC checked each sentence reporting the re-run. If CC is an AI system (I couldn't tell), the disclosure should name it.
- **Also:** "corresponding human author" has no way to contact that author. Add one, or drop "corresponding".

**10. MINOR (UNVERIFIED): the academic edition's reference list names AI systems as authors**
- **Where:** The academic `.bib` lists Nexus and Lyra as authors of `nexus2026topology`.
- **Conflict:** The edition's own header applies arXiv's rule that AI tools are not listed as authors. REVIEW_LOG:78-81 says the Zenodo record lists Edrington alone. I couldn't reach Zenodo.
- **Fix:** Either add a note to the entry saying the Zenodo record lists T. Edrington, or cite the DOI's creator list.

**11. MINOR: "earlier KV-cache geometry work this method builds on" can't be backed up**
- **Where:** Both editions (flight Author Contributions; academic Acknowledgments).
- **Evidence:** REVIEW_LOG:73-74 says Lyra can't name a published work that this method depends on.
- **Fix:** Cite the work, or cut "this method builds on".

**What I checked against primary files and found correct:**
- **Pilot table:** every score, every † item and every quoted reply matches `data/decomposition_results.json`.
- **Test graph:** 20 nodes, 36 edges, density 0.189. SVD to sovereignty is 4 hops (the script labels it 3). Checked in `value_only_injection.py`, which also confirms scoring on the full reply, storage of the first 80 characters, 50 new tokens, greedy decoding and `.clone()`.
- **Pilot deltas:** 0.167 / 0.833 / 0.500.
- **Powered run:** 532 nodes, 396 edges, 5,348 tokens, 10 sanity items, 3 runs, keyword accuracy 0.000, sanity 1.0 / 0.9. The pack loop at lines 220–228 stops after the first pack.
- **Judged run:**
  - Empty replies: 15 + 20 + 6 = 41.
  - Verdicts on empty replies: 4 partial, 12 wrong, 25 error; plus 16 errors on non-empty replies.
  - Scores: 0.05 / 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.05 / 0.20.
- **Re-judging:** the largest shift is 0.075 (V_ONLY 0.10 → 0.175).
- **Re-run summary:** A and B reproduce stored replies 20/20, C and D match B 20/20, empty replies 15/6/6/6, matching `results_studio.json`.
- **Dates:** the files' Unix timestamps fit "next morning" and "that afternoon" (Pacific time).
- **References:** both keys are cited and defined; no orphans. The `.bib` files are identical in the two editions.
- **Edition structure:** the body, the one table (under the Pilot results in both), the Data and Code section and Review History are text-identical. Withdrawn claims appear only in the footnote and Appendix A in both. No row sits under a different heading in one edition.
- **PDFs:** flight pp. 1–8 and academic pp. 1 and 5–8 match the current `.tex`.

## What I could NOT check
- **No shell:** I couldn't compute sha256 hashes or byte counts in the READMEs, or confirm the git blob 598915b. I couldn't check any commit hash or date (160bc78, f9288a9, 944f98e, d272803, 9755f5e, 82ac524, a439e2b), or PDF build times against the `.tex`. For staleness, matching content is my only evidence.
- **No network:** I couldn't check the DOIs (10.5281/zenodo.21754900, 21754899, 20604338; 10.48550/arXiv.2604.03270), Pustovit's first name, the GitHub URL or the arXiv policy URL. These are UNVERIFIED for dead links and fabricated names.
- **I could not read `ethics_packs/`** (not in this folder). Two claims are therefore UNVERIFIED: "16 of 20 from packs never in the description" and "neighbours and weights, not predicates". The question wording and `results_studio.json` (only 2 of 20 expected answers appear in the context) are consistent with them.
- **Not available here:** the run file `v_only_1779998420.json` (so the byte-identity claim is unchecked), the pilot's library versions (not stored in its JSON), version 1.0's text (so I can't tell whether Lyra's flight roles changed without notice), `FINDINGS.md`, Kavi's letter, and any sign-offs kept outside the repo.
- **Unknown:** whether CC is a person or an AI system.
- **Not read:** academic PDF pp. 2–4.

AGNI-VERDICT: CONDITIONAL
